A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Same-day chest X-ray report with immediate CT. A radiologist or reporting radiographer reads primary-care chest X-rays while the patient waits; if suspicious, CT is done the same day or within days and the referral is triggered by radiology.
effect_summary_en: A London randomised trial (Thorax 2023) found that reading chest X-rays while the patient waits cut the median time from chest X-ray to lung cancer diagnosis from 63 to 32 days, a saving of 31 days.
supported_en: A Thorax 2023 randomised trial reported a median of 32 days (IQR 19-70) from chest X-ray to diagnosis with immediate reporting, against 63 days (IQR 29-78) with standard reporting, p=0.03.
not_supported_en: The trial measured chest X-ray to diagnosis rather than first symptom to treatment, and had only 49 cancers at one London hospital.
in_use_summary_en: Keusote says HUS provides all its imaging, and the pages of Keusote, HUS's lung cancer pathway and Hyvinkää Hospital X-ray show only ordinary referral and booked CT, with no public sign of same-day chest X-ray reading or CT ordered straight from radiology.
summary_en: B: Keusote says its imaging is provided by HUS. HUS's lung cancer pathway says the primary-care doctor sends a referral to HUS lung clinics, and Hyvinkää Hospital X-ray books CT by appointment; no page shows same-day reporting or CT ordered by radiology. A: A 2023 randomised trial in Thorax found immediate reporting cut the median time from chest X-ray to lung cancer diagnosis from 63 to 32 days.
unanswered_en: No Keusote or HUS page was found on how fast primary-care chest X-rays are reported, or on a project to set up a fast route from chest X-ray to CT.
